title: Orbital-selective electronic modes induced by doping and originating from distinct spin excitations: an essential feature of orbital-selective Mott transition
abstract: The nature of the orbital-selective Mott transition (OSMT) remains elusive. This study shows that, by doping an orbitally degenerate spin-1 antiferromagnetic insulator in the Kanamori-Hubbard model, electronic modes emerge in the band gap in an orbital-selective manner, exhibiting momentum-shifted spin-mode dispersion relations. Electronic modes originating from conventional spin excitations, including the low-energy one, appear in the doped orbital, while those from inter-orbital spin excitations appear in the undoped orbital. These emergent modes constitute an essential feature of the OSMT.
summary: This theoretical study investigates the Orbital-Selective Mott Transition (OSMT) in a spin-1 antiferromagnetic insulator using the Kanamori-Hubbard model. The authors demonstrate that doping induces orbital-selective electronic modes in the band gap. These emergent modes are fundamentally linked to distinct spin excitations—low-energy modes in the doped orbital and inter-orbital modes in the undoped orbital—providing a key signature of the OSMT.
main_problem: The study aims to elucidate the fundamental nature of the Orbital-Selective Mott Transition (OSMT) in correlated electron systems.
main_result: The OSMT is characterized by the emergence of orbital-selective electronic modes in the band gap upon doping, which are directly traceable to distinct spin excitation mechanisms in different orbitals.
method: The research employs theoretical analysis using the Non-Abelian Dynamical Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DDMRG) method applied to the Kanamori-Hubbard model.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a spin-1 antiferromagnetic insulator described by the Kanamori-Hubbard model (KHM) in one dimension, incorporating orbital degeneracy and Hund's coupling.
key_observables: Spectral function ($A_m^\delta(k, \omega)$), momentum distribution function ($n_m^\delta(k)$), and dynamical spin structure factors ($S^\pm_\delta(k, \omega)$ and $T^\pm_\delta(k, \omega)$).
important_parameters: Doping concentration ($\delta$), and coupling ratios like $U/t_1$, $U'/t_1$, and $J_H/t_1$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ground state at half filling has zero momentum and total spin, and that the overlap between added-electron states and spin-excited states is significant.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the emergence of doping-induced dispersion relations in the spectral function for both orbitals, comparing the undoped and doped ground states to spin-excited states.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the KHM model and the problem of OSMT, develops the theoretical framework using DDMRG, presents results showing orbital-selective mode emergence linked to spin excitations, and concludes by confirming this feature as essential to the OSMT.
why_interesting: The explicit link drawn between emergent electronic modes and underlying spin excitations provides a concrete, calculable mechanism for understanding Mott transitions in multiorbital systems, which is highly relevant to strongly correlated materials studied in AMO/condensed matter.
